articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ investment in the KC Current is creating an impact that reaches well beyond professional soccer. Through the club’s partnership with the University of Missouri-Kansas City, members of the women’s soccer team recently gained direct access to professional players and the lessons that come with life at the highest level. The mentorship session with KC Current player Haley Hopkins gave the Roos a chance to ask honest questions about pressure, confidence, training and life after college. For student-athletes balancing academics with competition, the experience offered something a classroom cannot easily provide: a closer look at what it takes to build a career in sport.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ KC Current partnershipThe KC Current has become an important part of Kansas City’s growing women’s sports scene. Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes are among the club’s ownership group, giving the Chiefs power couple a direct connection to an organisation that continues to invest in women’s soccer.That connection is now helping create opportunities for the next generation. The UMKC partnership brings professional experience closer to student-athletes, allowing players to learn from athletes who have already faced many of the challenges they are navigating.Hopkins spoke about her path from youth soccer and college competition to the National Women’s Soccer League. Her advice focused on practical issues such as preparation, confidence and managing life away from the pitch.For senior health sciences major Maddie Muhr, the experience carried lessons that will last longer than a season.“I feel lucky to have this opportunity,” Muhr said. “I haven’t heard of any other program that gets to be so closely tied with another amazing program like the KC Current. articles.title: "Scores 6s on the field, 3s off the field": Raiders fan takes a nasty dig at Travis Kelce's married life
articles.summary: If there is one thing NFL fans love almost as much as touchdowns, it is finding a creative new way to roast an opposing team.
articles.body: If there is one thing NFL fans love almost as much as touchdowns, it is finding a creative new way to roast an opposing team. And one Las Vegas Raiders fan apparently decided that Travis Kelce’s relationship with Taylor Swift was fair game.Taylor Swift dragged into Raiders-Chiefs rivalry as fan trolls Travis Kelce with viral signDuring the Chiefs-Raiders showdown, the fan was spotted in the stands holding up a sign featuring photos of Kelce and Swift alongside a message that read: “Scores 6s on the field… 3s off the field.” Yep. A Raiders’ fan went there.The joke is built around one of football’s simplest numbers. A touchdown is worth six points, making “6s on the field” an easy reference to Kelce’s job as one of the NFL’s most recognizable tight ends. The “3s off the field” part, however, was clearly aimed at his superstar romance with Swift.In other words, the fan was basically giving Kelce a very questionable scouting report on his married life. And considering this was a Raiders-Chiefs rivalry game, subtlety was never really going to be part of the game plan.Kelce and Swift have been one of the most talked-about celebrity couples in the world since their relationship became public, making the Chiefs tight end an especially easy target for opposing fans. Swift wasn't even the one standing in the stadium, but somehow she still managed to make it onto a Raiders fan's game-day sign.The fan's sign quickly caught attention online, with the image making the rounds as fans reacted to the rather creative and very nasty attempt to get inside Kelce's head.The joke landed, but the Chiefs had the final wordThere was one small problem with the Raiders fan's trolling strategy: Kansas City still walked away with the win. The Chiefs defeated Las Vegas 30-27 in the Week 4 matchup, improving to 4-0 while the Raiders dropped to 3-1. Kelce himself had a relatively quiet night statistically, finishing with two catches for 15 yards and no touchdown.So while the Raiders fan may have won the battle of the signs, the Chiefs ultimately won the battle that mattered. articles.summary: Brittany Mahomes clearly wasn’t planning on letting the Chiefs-Raiders showdown be the only thing turning heads in Las Vegas.
articles.body: Brittany Mahomes clearly wasn’t planning on letting the Chiefs-Raiders showdown be the only thing turning heads in Las Vegas. While cheering on husband Patrick Mahomes at Allegiant Stadium, Brittany stepped out in a seriously bold game-day outfit that brought a whole new meaning to “dress for the occasion.”Brittany Mahomes turns heads in nearly $8,000 snakeskin look at Chiefs gameThe 31-year-old showed off a head-to-toe snakeskin-inspired look that reportedly cost nearly $8,000 because apparently regular jeans simply weren’t dramatic enough for a Chiefs game. The statement look came courtesy of Stella McCartney, with Brittany sporting a brown snakeskin-patterned bomber jacket over a simple white tank top. But the real conversation starter was happening below the waist.Rather than wearing ordinary leather pants, Brittany paired her blue jeans with matching snakeskin chaps, creating a denim-meets-Western-meets-high-fashion combination that was impossible to miss. The chaps are part of Stella McCartney’s Winter 2025 collection and feature panels made from YATAY M, the designer’s vegan alternative to exotic animal skins that uses mycelium, the root-like structure of fungi.And these were definitely not your average pair of jeans. Stella McCartney originally listed the Snake Panel Chaps Denim Jeans at $1,790, while the designer’s coordinating crocodile-embossed bomber jacket has been listed at $3,990 in the U.S. Brittany finished the look with brown pointed-toe heels, silver earrings and a diamond ring, while keeping her blonde hair in loose waves pulled back into a half-up style. Her makeup was equally polished, with smoky brown eyes, glossy lips and a glowy complexion.So, yes, Brittany essentially showed up to watch football wearing thousands of dollars worth of vegan snakeskin-inspired fashion, and somehow made the chaps look like a perfectly reasonable thing to wear from the luxury suite. But the outfit wasn't the only thing Brittany had fun with that night.After the Chiefs completed a wild 30-27 comeback win over the Raiders, Brittany posted photos of her game-day look alongside a cheeky caption quoting Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak's halftime confidence: “We’re winning. We’re gonna win the game.” The Raiders, unfortunately for Kubiak, had other plans.Kansas City came roaring back in the fourth quarter, Patrick Mahomes led three touchdown drives, and Brittany got the perfect opportunity to let the outfit and the caption do some talking. Nearly $8,000 outfit. Snakeskin chaps. A comeback win. And a little postgame trolling. articles.title: How Brittany Mahomes helped turn Patrick Mahomes from a small-town Texas kid into the most grounded superstar in the NFL
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes has three Super Bowl rings, two MVP awards, and one of the biggest contracts in sports history.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes has three Super Bowl rings, two MVP awards, and one of the biggest contracts in sports history. Yet the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback still carries himself like the kid from Whitehouse, Texas. Much of that, he has often suggested, traces back to Brittany Mahomes. They met in high school, stayed together through the draft and the fame, and married in 2022. She is now the mother of his children and a co-owner of an NWSL club. Here is how their bond shaped the quarterback fans see today.How did Brittany Mahomes help Patrick Mahomes stay grounded?Brittany knew Patrick long before the highlights, the rings, or the endorsement deals. They started dating at Whitehouse High School, back when he was a multi-sport athlete with a baseball future in mind and she was a soccer player. That shared history matters. When a quarterback becomes a global name, most people around him meet the finished product. Brittany met the teenager.She stayed beside him through the Texas Tech years, the 2017 draft that sent him to Kansas City at No. 10, and a rookie season spent mostly behind Alex Smith. That kind of patience comes easier when someone already believes in you.The grounding shows up in small ways. Patrick talks about family first in postgame interviews. His kids, Sterling and Bronze, are regular visitors on the field after big wins. Brittany is a constant presence at Arrowhead, cheering loudly and rarely hiding it.The picture is less about glamour and more about routine. Fame can warp a young star's circle fast. His has stayed small and familiar, and both of them seem to protect that.How has family life changed Patrick Mahomes on and off the field?The biggest shift came with fatherhood. Sterling arrived in 2021 and Bronze in 2022, and Patrick has talked openly about how being a dad puts football in perspective. You can see it after losses. His answers are calm and short, and he moves on to the next week without the long brooding some stars are known for.Brittany has built her own lane too. She is a co-owner of the Kansas City Current, the NWSL club that opened CPKC Stadium in 2024, billed as the first stadium built specifically for a women's pro team. For the couple, that means ties to Kansas City that go beyond Patrick's playing days. They have a stake in the city's sports future, and in women's sport as a whole.Life at that level also brings noise. Brittany draws plenty of attention on social media, and not all of it is kind. The couple mostly lets it pass. Their focus stays on the field, the kids and the next game.Whether that steadiness lasts another decade of fame is a fair question. articles.title: After Impressing Celtics Teammates, Baylor Scheierman Eyes Bigger Role
articles.summary: Baylor Scheierman is ready to show what he can really do with the Celtics if given the opportunity.
articles.body:
Baylor Scheierman earned more opportunities in his second season with the Celtics last year. He found confidence and took advantage when those opportunities arose. Now, he aims to build on that.

Entering year three, Scheierman is in a unique situation. The Celtics traded Jaylen Brown to the 76ers for Paul George. Boston also signed Mike Conley. Jayson Tatum is the leader, while Payton Pritchard looks to have another breakout season.

The shooter, who played for South Dakota State and Creighton, has been training hard heading into the 2026-27 season, and star players and veterans, like Conley and Pritchard, have taken notice.

"The other day, Baylor, I think I got like four offensive rebounds in one possession, and I just said, 'I like him,'" Conley told SI . "Like that's all I need to know. I like him. I like him a lot. And obviously, he did a bunch of other things other than that. But his willingness to crash and keep possessions alive and make the right reads was impressive. Stuff like that sticks out to me."

"He's been really good," Pritchard said. "Like just really good in the areas, like the margins. His game's grown. Obviously, he's always been a good shooter, good floater, stuff like that. But he will be really important for this team this year."

The former Summit League Player of the Year and All-Big East honoree was selected with the 30th pick by the Celtics in the 2024 NBA Draft. In 31 games during the 2024-25 season, Scheierman averaged 3.6 points, 2.1 rebounds, 1.1 assists, and 0.5 steals per game. In 77 games last season, he averaged 5.5 points, 3.5 rebounds, 1.5 assists, and 0.5 steals per game.

Given the chance to prove himself, Scheierman increased his value. He's ready to do that in preseason play. Scheierman appreciates those who give him his flowers. The 26-year-old is ready to show what he can really do if given the opportunity.

"It's really about attacking every single day, and with whatever opportunity you get, kind of making the most of it," Scheierman said. "You start the year not really knowing what's going to happen, and you get a little opportunity here, you try to make the most of it, and with that, more opportunity comes.

"And so, whatever opportunity I'm given, I have the most confidence in myself that I'll be able to impact the game in whatever way."

articles.title: Sean McVay Comments on Rams Coaches Giving Middle Finger, Yelling at Eagles Fans in Viral Videos
articles.summary: Some Los Angeles Rams coaches caught flak this week after provoking Philadelphia Eagles fans during a 24-20 win, and head coach Sean McVay addressed the situation on Monday.
articles.body:
Some Los Angeles Rams coaches caught flak this week after provoking Philadelphia Eagles fans during a 24-20 win, and head coach Sean McVay addressed the situation on Monday.

McVay said that he spoke with the assistant coaches about their behavior and said, "We'll be better in those situations," per ESPN's Sarah Barshop .

After trailing by 10 points with just over eight minutes to go, the Rams managed to cut the deficit to three points with just under four minutes remaining before taking the lead with a touchdown with just over a minute to play.

A handful of coaches appeared to be banging on the windows and making gestures at the Eagles' fans after taking the lead and during Philadelphia's final drive. Some fans responded by shouting back at the coaches and even throwing items at the windows.

McVay was a coordinator at Washington before taking over in Los Angeles, and he said being close to the fans can make "you excited and emotional."

Still, McVay doesn't want his coordinators to repeat what they did on Sunday.

"We'll learn from that," McVay said. "We'll be better. Those fans are really into it, but I know that we want to make sure that we're representing the class and just the calm steadiness that we want to have while also being emotionally into it. And there's ways that we can have that reflected.

"We did talk about it, and that won't be an issue moving forward."

The Rams improved to 2-2 with the come-from-behind win and will look to carry the momentum into next week's contest against the Buffalo Bills. They'll be back in Los Angeles, so there likely won't be any back-and-forth between coordinators and fans.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels Injury Update, Return Timeline Provided by HC Before Commanders vs. Giants
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders are off to a 1-3 start this season, but they received some welcome news as they look to turn things around going into their Week 5 game against the New York Giants.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders are off to a 1-3 start this season, but they received some welcome news as they look to turn things around going into their Week 5 game against the New York Giants.

Head coach Dan Quinn told reporters Monday the team expects Jayden Daniels to return from his dislocated left elbow for the upcoming game.

"The goal is for him to have a full week of practice, a full week and start on Sunday," Quinn said.

Daniels suffered the injury during Washington's Week 2 loss to the Dallas Cowboys but returned to practice ahead of the Week 4 game against the Indianapolis Colts.

While he didn't play, he traveled with the team to London and seemed to be making strides toward a return to the field. And Quinn confirmed the plan is for him to be back in the lineup for an important divisional contest.

Marcus Mariota led the Commanders to a win over the Seattle Seahawks in Week 3 but suffered an MCL injury against the Colts. That forced the team to turn toward seventh-round draft pick Athan Kaliakmanis, which surely wasn't the plan coming into the campaign.

Kaliakmanis threw a handful of impressive deep passes, but he also threw an interception and struggled at times against the Indianapolis defense in a 30-13 loss.

Washington needs Daniels back and healthy if it is going to overcome its slow start and get back into the NFC East race. He was the Offensive Rookie of the Year and a Pro Bowler in his first season in 2024 but was limited to just seven games last season.

He is dealing with injury concerns again this year, although ESPN's John Keim reported last week the plan is for the quarterback to wear a different brace this time around that "keeps his elbow slightly bent to prevent another dislocation."

The Commanders need a victory over the Giants because they face the San Francisco 49ers, Philadelphia Eagles and Los Angeles Rams in a daunting stretch of three games after playing New York.

If they lose to the divisional foe, the season may slip away from them even with Daniels back under center.

articles.title: Marcus Davenport Retires 1 Day After Bears Debut, Former Saints 1st-Round Pick Spent 9 Years in NFL
articles.summary: Marcus Davenport made his Chicago Bears debut on Sunday. On Monday, he decided to call it a career.
articles.body:
Marcus Davenport made his Chicago Bears debut on Sunday. On Monday, he decided to call it a career.

Per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo, the veteran pass rusher has decided to retire after nine years in the NFL and has asked for a release from the Bears.

Davenport, 30, signed with the Bears in August but did not make the 53-man roster because he was still ramping up when the team had to make its final cuts. He then joined the team's practice squad before making his debut on Sunday.

In his only game with Chicago, Davenport logged a tackle in a 23-12 win over the New York Jets.

Davenport was drafted 14th overall by the New Orleans Saints, making him the only first-round pick to come out of UTSA. He spent his first five seasons with the Saints, including the best year of his career in 2021, when he logged 39 tackles, nine sacks and three forced fumbles.

He signed a one-year deal with the Minnesota Vikings in 2023 but played just four games before suffering a season-ending ankle injury, starting a stretch of bad injury luck for him.

Davenport spent the 2024 and 2025 campaigns with the Detroit Lions, but played just 10 games total because of various injuries. He went into the 2026 season perhaps hoping to get back on track after several injury-riddled years, but he ultimately decided to hang it up.

Davenport finishes his career with 165 tackles, 25 sacks and seven forced fumbles.

articles.title: After 15 years with ALS, Saints legend Steve Gleason reveals how his diagnosis changed his life and strengthened his connection with NFL players
articles.summary: New Orleans Saints legend Steve Gleason is marking 20 years since one of the most important plays in franchise history while reflecting on a very
articles.body: New Orleans Saints legend Steve Gleason is marking 20 years since one of the most important plays in franchise history while reflecting on a very different battle that began five years later. Gleason was diagnosed with ALS in 2011, but the blocked punt he made against the Atlanta Falcons in 2006 eventually became much more than a defining football moment. In an interview with ABC News’ Robin Roberts, Gleason explained how that play helped give him a public platform for Team Gleason and connected him with other NFL players facing ALS. Now, 15 years into his diagnosis, he says his life still holds plenty of meaning.How did Steve Gleason’s 2006 blocked punt shape his life?Gleason’s place in Saints history was secured during the team’s first home game at the Superdome after Hurricane Katrina. On Sept. 25, 2006, he blocked Michael Koenen’s punt in the first quarter against Atlanta. Curtis Deloatch recovered the ball in the end zone, giving New Orleans its first touchdown in a 23-3 victory.The play became one of the defining images of the city’s return. Gleason understood its importance that night, but he later realized the moment had also changed his own future.“If I do not block that punt, I am another former special teams player, a has-been football guy," Gleason said. "When the ALS came I probably fade away quietly and die anonymously."He believes the visibility from that play eventually helped Team Gleason, the nonprofit he founded in 2011 to support people living with ALS.“That play made me visible at the exact moment this city needed a symbol. Years later, that visibility became a lifeline.”What has life been like for Gleason after his ALS diagnosis?Gleason has now lived with ALS for 15 years. The disease has taken away his ability to move, speak and breathe independently, but he remains closely involved with his family, creative work and advocacy.“I cannot move, talk, or breathe on my own. Some days are brutal," Gleason said, speaking with Roberts. "And still, this is a miraculous, wonderful life. ... I wake up, I watch the sunrise, I am with [my wife] Michel, [kids] Rivers and Gray. I get to love this life and the people in it."He communicates with his eyes using a specialized tablet, with eye tape helping him keep his eyebrows positioned correctly.“I live on a ventilator," Gleason explained. "I live knowing this breath is given to me by a machine, and this sentence is built letter by letter, and this moment with those I love is the whole point."That perspective has also shaped the way he talks about survival.“Robin, I'm still here. That still surprises some people," Gleason told ABC News' Robin Roberts. "It does not surprise me as much as it used to."Why does Gleason call other NFL players with ALS his brothers?Gleason has found another source of strength through former NFL players who have also dealt with ALS. He calls them his NFL “brothers,” including Chris Johnson, Tim Shaw, O.J. Brigance, Eric Stevens and Steve Smith.“Chris Johnson is my NFL brother. Tim Shaw, O.J. Brigance, Eric Stevens, Steve Smith, others," Gleason said. "More importantly, they are my fellow humans. When ALS enters your life, it is a tsunami of emotions. I want everyone in their families to know they are not alone."His message reaches beyond former players. Gleason wants families dealing with ALS to understand that the disease does not have to become an isolated experience.That sense of community has become a major part of his work with Team Gleason, which has used his public profile to raise awareness and provide support for people living with ALS.What does Gleason’s return to the Superdome mean now?Gleason will return to the Superdome with his family as the Saints mark the 20th anniversary of their return following Katrina. He and Deloatch will be honored as “Legends of the Game,” while Team Gleason will benefit from the game's 50/50 raffle.“When I roll back into that stadium, I will not only be visiting a monument to 2006, I will be walking into a mirror, a place that learned how to rise," Gleason said. "I had to learn the same thing. Twenty years later, I can't wait to be in the room where that love still lives."His connection to New Orleans has also extended into music. Gleason recently released “Rebirth,” an album combining his poetry with work from New Orleans musicians."It's a love letter to the people and spirit of this wild place," Gleason said of the project. "Who better to bring that to life than the best musicians from right here in New Orleans? When we started reaching out around town, they kept saying yes. Their support has been one of the most meaningful parts of making this album for me."The NFL has also announced a $500,000 donation to Answer ALS’ Champion Insights program, which studies ALS among professional football players, other elite athletes and military first responders.For Gleason, the meaning of that old blocked punt has changed with time. articles.title: Aaron Rodgers hints wife Brittani could be ‘pregnant’ as quarterback reveals a glimpse into their next chapter
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers may have offered his clearest hint yet that his life after football could include fatherhood.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers may have offered his clearest hint yet that his life after football could include fatherhood. During a Prime Video conversation with Al Michaels before the Pittsburgh Steelers faced the Cleveland Browns, Rodgers was asked where he expected to be a year from now. His answer immediately drew attention to his personal life. “I'll either be tending to my pregnant wife or I'll be taking care of my newborn,” Rodgers said. The comment has fueled speculation about wife Brittani, although neither Rodgers nor Brittani has publicly confirmed that they are expecting a child.Is Aaron Rodgers hinting that wife Brittani is pregnant?Rodgers’ wording was notable because he did not simply talk about spending more time with his wife after retirement. He specifically mentioned a “pregnant wife” and a “newborn,” giving fans a glimpse of what he sees as a possible future away from the NFL.The quarterback made the comment while speaking with Michaels ahead of Pittsburgh’s game against Cleveland. According to Sports Illustrated, Michaels asked Rodgers where he expected his life to be one year later. Rodgers responded with the line that has since sparked the pregnancy talk.Still, there is an important distinction here. Rodgers did not announce that Brittani is pregnant. The couple has not publicly confirmed a pregnancy, so his comment should be viewed as a hint rather than an official announcement. There is also the possibility that Rodgers was joking, something he has been known to do when discussing his private life with the media.That uncertainty is what makes the remark interesting. Rodgers chose a very specific scenario when asked to picture his life beyond football, and it involved his wife and a potential child.What does Aaron Rodgers’ comment mean for his life after football?Aaron Rodgers is already preparing for a major change regardless of whether his comment points to an actual pregnancy. The 42-year-old quarterback has said the 2026 season will be his 22nd and final NFL season. He signed a one-year deal with the Steelers in May, bringing him back for another season and reuniting him with Mike McCarthy, his former coach in Green Bay.For a player who has spent more than two decades building his life around football, retirement could bring a very different routine. Rodgers has now suggested that family could become a much bigger part of that picture.His answer also arrived at an interesting point in his career. Rather than talking about another season, another team or what might come next in football, Rodgers was asked to imagine an ordinary life a year removed from the sport.Whether the remark was playful or revealing, it gave fans something they rarely get from Rodgers: a small glimpse into what he wants his personal future to look like.For now, though, the key detail remains unchanged. articles.title: Falcons Beat Saints, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Penix, Shough, Bijan, London, Top Players
articles.summary: In a NFC South showdown, the Atlanta Falcons rode their dynamic Robinson duo at running back to a 45-24 victory over Tyler Shough and the New Orleans Saints on Monday night.
articles.body:
In a NFC South showdown, the Atlanta Falcons rode their dynamic Robinson duo at running back to a 45-24 victory over Tyler Shough and the New Orleans Saints on Monday night.

Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr. combined for five rushing touchdowns in a Monday night running back showdown as the Falcons outgained the Saints by 155 yards on the ground.

Panthers Offense Had Field Day In Win 😮‍💨

The Saints entered the matchup as 1.5-point home favorites over the Falcons, per FanDuel Sportsbook , but could not find an answer for Atlanta's ground game, falling to 1-3 while Atlanta improved to 2-2.

The Falcons struck first on a monster 59-yard touchdown run by Bijan Robinson, then closed out the quarter with another Bijan Robinson rushing score, this time from four yards out, to take a 14-0 lead after one.

Atlanta's defense set the tone, forcing New Orleans into a three-and-out, a missed 52-yard field goal and a fumble that gave the Falcons possession at the Saints' 22-yard line.

The Saints finally found their offense to open the second quarter, putting together a quick drive that ended with Alvin Kamara punching in New Orleans' lone score of the first half.

Atlanta answered immediately, with Brian Robinson adding a rushing touchdown before Nick Folk drilled a chip-shot field goal to send the Falcons into halftime with a 24-7 lead.

New Orleans ate up nearly half the clock in the third quarter, but the long drive finished in just three points

The Saints couldn't slow down Atlanta's ground game, as Brian Robinson powered in for his second rushing touchdown of the night to stretch the Falcons' lead to 31-10 headed into the final quarter.

The Saints opened the third quarter with Kamara's second rushing touchdown, attempting to chip away at Atlanta's lead.

The Falcons answered on the next possession, as Michael Penix Jr. threw his first touchdown pass of the night, connecting with Jahan Dotson for a 31-yard score extending their advantage to 21 points.

A turnover on downs set up a quick three-play touchdown drive for the Falcons—and, once again, Brian Robinson finished it off, extending Atlanta's lead and putting the game out of reach.

Shough's three-yard touchdown pass to Devaughn Vele with 1:13 remaining came too late, as Atlanta kneeled it out for a 21-point win.

Atlanta will host the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday for Sunday Night Football, with kickoff scheduled for 8:20 p.m. ET. New Orleans will host the Minnesota Vikings earlier that day, with kickoff set for 1:00 p.m. ET.

articles.title: NFL Power Rankings entering Week 5: Chiefs are all the way back at 4-0, though injury concerns linger
articles.summary: The Chiefs went 6-11 last season, which looks like an aberration.
articles.body:
NFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders NFC North : Bears | Lions | Packers | Vikings NFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers NFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks

AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets AFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers AFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers

Bad news for all those who thought the Kansas City Chiefs' dynasty was over.

The Chiefs might be an anomaly. No other NFL dynasty had a bad season in the middle of it. The Patriots missed the playoffs in 2008 a season after going 16-0, but they were 11-5 and missed on a tiebreaker. The 1982 49ers were 3-6, but that was a weird strike season. When any other NFL dynasty had a terrible season, the run was over at that point.

They're 4-0 after beating a Raiders team that was off to a 3-0 start. While there was plenty of faith in the Chiefs bouncing back this season, there were reasons to wonder as well. Kansas City went 6-11 last season, and that included 6-8 in Patrick Mahomes' starts. Mahomes tore his ACL on Dec. 14 and there was concern he wouldn't be available for the start of the season nine months later.

There were questions on the roster, not just the recurring issues at receiver but also losing three valuable starters from the secondary in free agency and a trade. Those questions have subsided. Mahomes looks healthy and pretty good. The excellence of free-agent addition Kenneth Walker at running back has given the Chiefs a dimension they haven't had in a long time. Kansas City is third in DVOA. It's fourth in EPA (expected points added per play) on offense and ninth in EPA allowed on defense; Chicago and Jacksonville are the only other teams ranked top nine in both.

Yet, there's concern. KC's receivers are now dealing with injuries. Tyquan Thornton, who was playing a big role because Xavier Worthy has done almost nothing in his third season, is out for months with a gruesome ankle injury . Rashee Rice suffered a hamstring injury on Sunday. The line has been without left tackle Josh Simmons all season due to injury. Walker is great but he has never had a huge workload in the NFL and will be asked to carry even more of the offense going forward. If Walker fades or gets injured, it could get scary.

But every team has concerns. For the Chiefs, all that matters is they are undefeated and with very promising balance through four weeks. There was a question after last season's stunning fall if the Chiefs' dynasty was over. The Chiefs have seemingly provided the answer to that.

Here are the NFL power rankings after Week 4 of the NFL season:

The Dolphins battled at Minnesota, and if they didn't get unlucky on Chris Bell barely stepping out of bounds before catching a long touchdown and getting an illegal touching penalty, maybe they'd have a win. But it's another loss, and Miami's offense is still hard to watch. Unfortunately for Dolphins fans, it's a familiar feeling.

The problem might be that the Dolphins can't really get an evaluation of Malik Willis. He has not played well. He had 85 yards passing and was inaccurate on several throws. But given the junior varsity roster around him, is he getting a fair look? The Dolphins need to figure it out before the 2027 NFL Draft, though it seems inevitable they'll be taking a quarterback.

Maybe it was just a half of garbage time with the Ravens trying to just run out the clock without Lamar Jackson after halftime, but there were some signs of progress from the Titans.

They outscored Baltimore 11-0 in the second half. Cam Ward finished 20-of-31 passing for 222 yards and a touchdown. Carnell Tate might have been the biggest story for Tennessee, as the fourth overall pick of the draft had nine catches for 145 yards. In the first three weeks combined he had 13 catches for 123 yards. There were still issues. Tate fumbled twice, losing one. Ward threw an interception on a flip pass that went off Tony Pollard's hands and Tennessee had just one scoring drive in the first half as Baltimore pulled away. Tennessee gave up 24 points in the first half. But at least it was a little better in the second half.

"We have to really hone in on the bad plays, and how we can limit that," Ward said, via the team's site . "We have to limit the bad plays on both sides of the ball, not just offense."

At some point, Buccaneers ownership will ask how the team put itself in a position that it had to start undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels at quarterback with its season slipping away. Daniels was the first undrafted rookie QB to start a game in Week 4 or earlier since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger. Daniels did the best he could in a tough situation, completing 19-of-27 passing for 148 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions with 55 yards rushing. But the Buccaneers came up short, scoring only 14 points.

Head coach Todd Bowles is firmly on the hot seat . General manager Jason Licht did a great job constructing the 2020 Bucs team that won a title, but Tampa Bay's record is 93-108 in his 13 seasons as GM. If this season continues to get worse with Daniels starting, or even with Baker Mayfield rushing back from a thumb injury, nobody should feel too safe.

Maybe the second half, when the Chargers outscored Seattle 17-10, is a sign that things are turning around. Probably not though. Seattle led 20-6 at halftime. Herbert was 5 of 14 for 36 passing yards and two interceptions with a passer rating of 4.8 at halftime. Seattle let its guard down in the second half and allowed LA to have a shot at tying the game in the final two minutes. With the game on the line, the Seahawks sacked Herbert, causing a fumble the Chargers lost. That seemed more like the 2026 Chargers.

The Chargers lost their last three games last season, including one in the playoffs. The seven-game losing streak is the longest of Jim Harbaugh's entire coaching career in college or the pros, according to NFL Media researcher John Todd . Harbaugh should turn things around. But it's possible the Chargers are buried by the time that happens.

We might be seeing the Jets start to unravel. They've lost three in a row since beating the Titans in Week 1, and Sunday's performance was miserable for them. They ran just 32 plays compared to 89 for the Bears, a massive discrepancy. The last time there was a gap that large was when the 1999 Browns, an expansion team, ran 28 plays to 90 for the Steelers ( h/t FootballPerspective.com ).

Late in the third quarter, Geno Smith was 5-for-11 passing for 44 yards. The Jets had some offensive injuries but the Bears were using their backup quarterback, so it's not a great excuse.

The Jets' offense has looked much better than that this season so perhaps it was just a truly horrible afternoon. But at 1-3, the season could get away from New York quickly.

Jeremiyah Love's comments after the fourth game of his rookie season were odd. Love played 30 snaps, six fewer than Tyler Allgeier, and the Cardinals lost a game that was up in the air until the final play. It was weird usage. Love said he was being managed and he was good with it. He said he would "probably just hinder the team" playing more and he said he told the coaches, "I think Tyler or Bam [Knight] can exert themselves a little bit more," according to ESPN's Josh Weinfuss . Love said the high-ankle sprain he had in preseason isn't an issue anymore, just general wear and tear and management by coaches.

"It's been a long year for me," Love said, via Weinfuss. "Body sometimes is down, body sometimes is tired. So it's just managing those things. Coaches know that this is probably going to be the longest year of my life. And just want to manage that workload."

Love tweaked his other ankle in Sunday's loss , head coach Mike LaFleur said Monday, raising the need to manage the rookie's workdload.

Love was the third overall pick of the NFL Draft and has looked good (4.1 yards per carry) even though his snaps have been limited. The Cardinals shouldn't be running the third pick into the ground when it's clear they're not a playoff contender, but it's still unusual to hear Love talking about how it has already been a long year when the Cardinals still have 13 games to go.

With 2:23 left on Sunday, the Texans scored to take a 30-27 lead. A defense that was expected to be one of the best in the NFL could win the game with one stop, or at least make sure the game went to overtime by holding Dallas to a field goal. The Cowboys went downfield and scored a touchdown.

Dallas has a good offense but Houston was supposed to have a good defense. The Texans don't. They are surprisingly average: 14th in DVOA after Sunday's games and 26th in EPA ( expected points added ) allowed per play. Defensive dominance can vary more season to season than offensive excellence, but it's still surprising that the Texans are winless and a middle-of-the-road defense is a big reason for that.

"It sucks, because we know we're the ones out there on the field," Texans cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. said, via the Houston Chronicle . "The coaches put us in the right position to win and we've got to do it. They can't do it, we've got to do it. We've got great coaches, we've got great everybody. We've got to go out there and do our job."

Maybe if Marcus Mariota hadn't gotten injured, the Commanders might have won and been a promising 2-2. They were about to take an early 6-0 lead on the Colts early in the game when Mariota sprained MCL in his right knee. The Commanders' defense played pretty well but Washington's offense couldn't do much with rookie Athan Kaliakmanis in for Mariota and an inactive Jayden Daniels. And 1-3 is a tough hole to dig out of.

With Mariota hurt and the Commanders in danger of having their season slip away further, there has to be tremendous urgency for Daniels to return from a dislocated left elbow.

"That's the hope for us for sure, Jay coming back," Commanders coach Dan Quinn said . "He'll have a full week of practice Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. That's the goal: that he could get into that space."

The Packers won. They faced an undrafted rookie quarterback making his first start and escaped with a 17-14 victory when the Buccaneers threw incomplete on fourth-and-11 from the Packers' 47-yard line. That's not exactly the dominant performance that will get Packers fans off Matt LaFleur's back.

But a win is a win. Green Bay comes home and plays the Bears in Week 5 , a game that was flexed out of the late afternoon time slot in part because of Caleb Williams' injury but also because the Packers aren't that interesting. A third straight loss to the Bears, including last season's horrid collapse in the wild-card round, will have Green Bay fans again calling for LaFleur's job.

It seemed like the Saints were off to a promising start to this season after the second half of last season went very well. But it doesn't look as good after Monday night's blowout loss to the Falcons. New Orleans is a fourth-quarter comeback against the Ravens from being 0-4. Its offensive line did a poor job protecting quarterback Tyler Shough, the running game without injured Travis Etienne Jr. was ineffective and the defense was picked apart by the Falcons.

The one concern about taking the Saints' hot finish to last season and projecting it to this season was that it came against weak competition. In Shough's starts last season, the Saints faced just one team with a winning record, and they lost that game 34-10 to the Rams. Almost beating the Lions and then defeating the Ravens made it look like the Saints would carry over their hot streak from last season. After blowing a game to the Raiders at home and being blown out by the Falcons, it looks more like that start was a mirage, and last season's second half was a product of a soft part of the schedule.

The Colts might have been lucky that the Commanders played most of Sunday's game in London with a third-string rookie quarterback. They did not play well. Daniel Jones' struggles are a real issue. He is 27th among 32 NFL quarterbacks in EPA per play. He is generating -0.065 EPA per play this season. His mark last season was 0.220, which was seventh among all QBs with at least 100 snaps. On Sunday, Jones had just 143 yards against one of the NFL's worst secondaries. He also had an interception and a lost fumble.

Injuries at receiver have been an issue. Missing Alec Pierce changes how defenses approach the Colts, without the threat of big plays downfield. Still, Jones looks much worse than he did last season and it's fair to wonder if his Achilles tear plays a part in that. He still has the support of Colts head coach Shane Steichen, who said Jones is doing a good job.

"I think he's done some really good things and then some things we need to clean up," Steichen told the media . "But he's made some big-time throws."

The days of this Steelers defense scaring anyone are probably over. Pittsburgh is 15th in defensive DVOA through Sunday's games, 14th in EPA allowed per play, 23rd in success rate allowed and 13th in yards per game allowed. Pittsburgh allowed Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson to go 14-of-17 passing for 181 yards and a touchdown in the first half last Thursday night, then let him put together a game-winning drive.

It's just an average defense. The Steelers had the second-oldest defense in the NFL coming into the season by average age, so it's not like there's an obvious turnaround coming with a young unit. The offense's upside is limited with a 42-year-old Aaron Rodgers at quarterback. The ceiling is not very high for this team.

Cleveland should be happy to be on a three-game winning streak. It's probably not sustainable. The Browns have had three very close wins, with the go-ahead scores coming with 3:51, 1:48 and 10 seconds to play. Their point differential is -14. Their DVOA is 23rd.

And still, it's OK to be excited. The young cast around the quarterback position is flashing a lot of talent. Rookie receivers Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion Jr. already look good, and second-year tight end Harold Fannin Jr. is playing well again this season. Deshaun Watson is still very unlikely to be the long-term answer at quarterback but if the Browns get that right in the 2027 NFL Draft, the future is bright. And the Browns are at the Jets next, so a 4-1 start is possible.

"This ain't the old Browns," Cleveland defensive end Jared Verse said, according to Cleveland.com . "We've got new swag."

Detroit's defense isn't good enough to make the Lions scary to anyone. Detroit is allowing 423.8 yards per game, and no other NFL team is giving up more than 392.3. Detroit has allowed 127 points, most in the NFL. On Sunday against the Panthers, Tetairoa McMillan torched the secondary for 192 yards and two touchdowns on 14 catches.

It's bad enough that head coach Dan Campbell was asked afterward if defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard could be relieved of his duties.

"I'm not talking about all that," Campbell told the media after Sunday's loss . "I'm talking about getting better right now, with what we've got, and that's what we're going to do. We're going to find a way to get better with what we've got."

Campbell might not want to talk about it, but the Lions aren't going anywhere with a defense this bad.

Bryce Young is having an unexpected breakout. It's not like Young didn't have talent. He was a Heisman Trophy winner and a No. 1 overall draft pick. But Young has gone from a low-volume quarterback who topped out at 3,011 passing yards in 16 games last season to the NFL's leader in passing yards through Sunday's games. He is averaging 317 passing yards per game, which would be 5,389 through 17 games. That would be the third-most passing yards in a single season in NFL history. Before this season Young had never averaged more than 188.2 yards per game over a full season. Young had three 300-yard games in his first three seasons, and he already has two through four games this season. It's unusual to have a quarterback take that big a leap in his fourth season.

He's off to such a hot start that the Sunday night television audience heard Panthers fans chanting "MVP" at their quarterback.

"Yeah, I heard it," Young said, via the Panthers' site. "In the moment, you're just focusing on executing and trying to move the team."

The Giants are winning and that's a testament to a much-improved coaching staff and some of the young talent. It'll be hard to keep it going. Jameis Winston had two turnovers and took four sacks in a win against a bad Cardinals team that came down to the final play. Winston has started 91 games in his career and has 116 interceptions. Everyone knows where this is headed. And those thinking J.J. McCarthy will be a big improvement haven't seen McCarthy play enough.

Still, the Giants are leading the NFC East. They needed an interception in their end zone with 17 seconds left to beat an 0-4 Titans team two weeks ago, and an interception at the 2-yard line on the final play to beat a 1-3 Cardinals team on Sunday. Both of those games were at home. But head coach John Harbaugh views the high-wire wins as a positive.

"That's what winning is," Harbaugh said, via the team's site . "That's what winning teams do. They find ways to win games. That's why they're winning teams and I'm proud of those guys for that."

It appears the first two games of the Falcons' season shouldn't count for much. The Falcons were down to their third option at quarterback and struggled badly with Cooper Rush running the offense. They went 0-2. If we just judge the Falcons since Michael Penix Jr. came back, then this ranking might be a little low. Atlanta looks like a completely different team. The Falcons have two prime-time, road blowout wins since Penix returned. They pounded the Packers in Week 3, winning 35-14, and then looked even better blasting the Saints on Monday night . The offense that looked so bad has taken off. It's not because Penix has been otherworldly, but he has been solid and defenses have to respect the Falcons' run game in a way they didn't when Rush was at quarterback. The Falcons' defense has been much better the last two weeks too. Defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich is a big reason the Falcons had a fantastic pass rush against Tyler Shough on Monday night. Maybe the NFC South will have a champion with a winning record after all.

The Eagles still haven't looked good this season. Barely beating the Commanders and Titans, who are a combined 1-7, isn't aging well. They were blown out by the Bears in Week 3 and then on Sunday blew a 10-point lead in the final five minutes. The Eagles did not score in the second half, the second straight game in which they were shut out after halftime. The Eagles were without receiver DeVonta Smith and tight end Dallas Goedert, who were inactive, and without running back Saquon Barkley for most of the game after he injured his hamstring. The Eagles also played without right tackle Lane Johnson, who was suddenly ruled out due to a personal matter on Sunday morning. It wouldn't be a surprise if Barkley misses some time, and there is no indication of what's going on with Johnson.

Despite all the excuses, the Eagles still have to be better than they were Sunday. They had 172 yards and went 0-for-12 on third downs. They averaged a putrid 3 yards per play. Jalen Hurts had 10 passing yards on 2 for 9 passing in the second half, which is stunningly bad no matter the opponent or injuries elsewhere.

"It hasn't been good enough," said Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni, who is getting a lot of heat in Philadelphia, according to the team's site .

The Broncos have played eight halves of football. They've been bad for six of them, particularly on offense. On Sunday, against a 49ers defense dealing with many injuries, Denver didn't score its first touchdown until 4:05 remained in the game. The Broncos are now 26th in offense in success rate. Denver is averaging 3.6 yards per rushing attempt, and only four teams are worse. The Broncos average 6.1 yards per pass attempt, and only three teams are worse than that.

The easy switch would be Sean Payton taking back play-calling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb. In Payton's first 18 seasons as a head coach between the Saints and Broncos, his offenses finished outside of the top 15 in yardage and points just three times. They're 27th in yardage and 26th in points scored this season. Payton declined to commit to a play-calling change in the aftermath of the latest offensive dud.

"It's too early," Payton said after Sunday's loss , according to transcripts. "It's a fair question; I appreciate it. It's tough to discuss any of that right now."

One big win changed the scope of the Patriots' season. They're right back in the AFC East race after beating the Bills. Drake Maye went from being berated for his poor play to a 269-yard, three-touchdown day. Receiver Romeo Doubs, who was looking like a free-agency bust after three games, made his impact with two touchdowns. A defense that hadn't been great did a good job limiting Josh Allen, and coming up with an interception with 1:05 to go and the Bills trailing by just three points.

One win, even one as crucial as Sunday's road victory, doesn't eliminate all concerns. But it's better than being three games behind Buffalo already this season.

"It gets us back in the race," head coach Mike Vrabel said, via the team's site . "We knew it was going to be a battle. Josh is unbelievable. Drake went toe-to-toe with him."

CeeDee Lamb had a game for the ages Sunday. He had 17 catches, and only six times in NFL history has a player had more. Lamb had 189 yards, making him the only Cowboy to have 17 catches and 170 yards in a game. He also caught the game-winning touchdown against the Texans with 40 seconds left.

"CeeDee's been great," QB Dak Prescott said., via the team's site .

Dallas still has a big defensive problem. The Cowboys are 31st in EPA allowed per play and there's a big gap between them and the Bills at No. 30. But the offense has mostly been as good as expected. And with the rest of the issues around the NFC East, Dallas is looking like the best team in the division.

The Bengals were off to such a good start at 2-0. And yet the Bengals still aren't over their slow starts. They lost to a flawed Steelers team and then couldn't pull off a late win against the Jaguars at home, dropping them to 2-2. This is the fifth straight season the Bengals have failed to be above .500 through four games.

The running game hasn't been helping. The Bengals have just 297 rushing yards through four games. Only the Packers are worse. They had to abandon it early Sunday. Cincinnati threw it 54 times and had just 12 rushing attempts by running backs. Chase Brown had just 10 yards on nine carries so it's not like the Bengals could trust the run game to sustain the offense. Brown has been productive since his 2024 breakout so it's likely he's just off to a slow start, like the Bengals as a team yet again.

Hindsight changes perceptions, but the Raiders taking a field goal off the board in the third quarter due to a defensive penalty and then failing to convert on fourth-and-2 was a critical turning point in a three-point loss to the Chiefs.

"We were going to be aggressive going into the game," Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said, according to the team's site . "I don't regret it. I regret not getting it."

Overall, the Raiders acquitted themselves just fine in defeat. They led with less than four minutes to play. They might have answered a late Chiefs touchdown, but they lost a fumble on the next kickoff. Las Vegas outgained the Chiefs 437-398, which is of little consolation but shows Vegas was close to knocking off Kansas City. If anything, the Raiders validated their hot start with a close loss to a Chiefs team that is 4-0 and has won nine of the last 10 AFC West titles.

The Vikings did something Sunday that no other team has accomplished since 1923. It's not great though. They're the first team since the 1923 Chicago Cardinals to start 4-0 and not score a touchdown in two of the wins.

The Vikings' offense has not been good. Not having Kyler Murray for a full game and most of a second is a reasonable excuse, as is missing Justin Jefferson for almost two full games. We'll see if the offense looks much better with Jefferson back and Murray healthy. But Murray hasn't been a very good NFL quarterback; the woebegone Cardinals took a dead salary cap hit of $54.7 million to be done with him. Even without Jefferson the Vikings should score at least one touchdown against a bad Dolphins defense at home (yes, T.J. Hockenson held up after getting a game-clinching first down when he could have scored, that's noted). Murray is last among NFL quarterbacks in success rate and second-to-last in EPA per play. Minnesota is going to take a step back if the offense doesn't get better, no matter how good the defense is.

It's tough to drop the Rams two spots after a road win against Philadelphia, but it's getting to a point where they have to play better to reclaim their status as an unquestionably elite team. The first three-plus quarters Sunday were ugly on offense. And that was with Puka Nacua back. Matthew Stafford has six touchdowns and six interceptions in four games. He had eight interceptions all of last season. Stafford is 38 years old and many quarterbacks see a steep decline in their late 30s, if they're still playing.

The Rams won because their defense was fantastic and then the offense came alive for two clutch drives at the end. A decision by the Eagles to go for it on fourth down instead of taking a short field goal to make the score 23-10 in the fourth quarter helped too. The Rams found a way to win but they've looked good in only one of four games, and that was after the Giants lost quarterback Jaxson Dart to injury in the first quarter. It doesn't get easier either: The Rams host the Bills next Monday night.

Everything is on hold as the Ravens find out if Lamar Jackson is OK from an ankle injury. Presumably, he was sitting in the second half mostly as a precaution, as the Ravens led 24-7 against a terrible Titans team. But any injury to Jackson's lower body is a concern considering how dangerous he is on the move.

Overall there's nothing wrong with the Ravens holding on to beat the Titans after they went in a shell without Jackson, though 13 penalties need to be addressed. They did enough to win, despite being outscored 11-0 in the second half, and that's all that matters. They didn't move down in these rankings as much as the Bears and Jaguars moved up past them. The Ravens are still a Super Bowl contender. But that depends on Jackson staying healthy. We saw in the second half what the Ravens would look like without Jackson, and it's not pretty.

The Bears get a big bump, and it's because of their defense. Chicago had a bad Week 1 on defense, and that seemed to be in line with its preseason expectations. The Bears were 25th in defensive DVOA last season and didn't make major improvements in the offseason. But over the last three weeks the Bears' defense has been excellent. From Week 2 through Week 4 they are third in EPA allowed per play. The only touchdowns they've given up in three weeks was an Eagles quarterback sneak that was snapped barely before time ran out in the first half, and a garbage time touchdown to the Jets in the fourth quarter when they led 23-6.

It helps that Chicago has faced the Vikings with Carson Wentz, an Eagles offense that looks surprisingly inept and the Jets, but the results are impressive. If Chicago has an above-average defense, this is a Super Bowl contender. We all know the offense will be fine, especially when Caleb Williams returns.

The Bills could have essentially finished the AFC East race. They were at home against the Patriots and could have exited that game with a three-game lead in the division. That's what made Sunday's loss a disappointment. Buffalo's defense in particular let down, allowing 405 yards to a New England offense that had been struggling.

Buffalo's offense is just fine, as it always will be with Josh Allen. Though Allen himself cost the team with an interception in the final two minutes that he admitted he should have thrown away instead of taking a risk downfield. The Bills' defense is the bigger issue. It is now 30th in EPA per play allowed and 26th in DVOA. The lowest a Super Bowl champion has ever ranked in defensive DVOA is the 2006 Colts at 25th. Either the Bills' defense needs to improve or Buffalo is in danger of wasting another season of Allen's prime.

The transitive property doesn't really work in the NFL but consider this: In Week 3, the Jaguars beat the Patriots 35-6. A week later that same Patriots team beat the Bills on the road. The easy takeaway from that, and how Jacksonville has looked in a season-plus of the Liam Coen era: The Jaguars have been underrated here and that needs to change. Coen is 16-5 as Jaguars head coach.

Jacksonville is second to San Francisco in DVOA , and that seems like the right spot. The Jags have blown out the Browns and Patriots, who are 5-1 against everyone else. They won at the Bengals, who had started the season 2-0 and are considered dangerous. The loss to the Broncos was unfortunate, but Jacksonville led 10-3 at halftime and it's not the first team to fade in the second half at altitude early in the season. Had it not been for that second half at Denver, Jacksonville would have a case to be the No. 1 team in these rankings. The Jaguars are very good.

If you want the Chiefs to fall off sometime soon, it's probably not going to happen. Their upcoming schedule is soft and should lead to a start of 8-2 or better:

Week 5: bye Week 6: vs. Chargers Week 7: at Seahawks Week 8: at Broncos Week 9: vs. Jets Week 10: at Falcons Week 11: vs. Cardinals

That's four games in which Kansas City should be significant favorites, and while the game at the Seahawks will be very tough, it's not like the Broncos are playing great. That's a winnable road game. A 4-2 run through those six games seems to be the worst outcome. The Chiefs aren't going away.

The Seahawks have been far from perfect. It was disappointing that they relaxed so much after taking a 27-6 lead against the Chargers that their defense had to get a stop in the final two minutes after Los Angeles cut the lead to 30-23. And it wasn't ideal that Seattle lost in Week 3 to the Commanders, who are 0-3 in their other games this season.

But there shouldn't be much concern about the Seahawks. The loss to the Commanders was fluky (they outgained Washington by 179 yards) and they won their other three games. The defense is still spectacular, ranking first in DVOA, even if it let up against the Chargers for a bit. Next up is a battle against the 49ers that likely will determine who is No. 1 in the Power Rankings after Week 5.

"Got to look forward, move forward. Got a big week ahead of us, and guys are excited," Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said, according to the team's site. "They played extremely hard, stayed together, and did enough to win the game, so we're thankful."

It has been a good runout for the 49ers. They haven't played a true road game yet. They faced the Cardinals and Dolphins, two of the NFL's worst teams. The weirdness of the Australia trip for the Rams has been talked about often. But the 49ers just keep winning and looking pretty good doing it.

If there's any remaining skepticism about the 49ers, this week will be telling. San Francisco plays at Seattle on Sunday afternoon. San Francisco's offense is first in the NFL in EPA per play and by a wide margin (0.274 with the Bills in second at 0.204). If the 49ers can keep that going against an excellent Seahawks defense, it will solidify the 49ers as the No. 1 team in the NFL so far this season.

articles.title: Saints DC 'Knew' They Would Struggle vs. Falcons amid Injuries, Troy Aikman Says
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons made light work of the New Orleans Saints' defense in a 45-24 win on Monday night.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons made light work of the New Orleans Saints' defense in a 45-24 win on Monday night.

According to ESPN analyst Troy Aikman, Saints defensive coordinator Brandon Staley knew what was coming.

"He doesn't have any answers, and I think he knew it when we talked to him," Aikman said during ESPN's Monday Night Football broadcast (h/t Saints Wire's John Sigler ). "I think he knew. He didn't tell us, but the guys that are out, some of their big edge rushers and guys who can play the run and set the edge, they're not on the field."

The Saints' defense was without a few key members, including edge rusher Carl Granderson, his backup Anfernee Jennings, and linebacker Kaden Elliss. That made for an easy day at the office for Atlanta's offense.

Running back Bijan Robinson had a monster game with 145 yards and two scores, and Brian Robinson Jr. rushed for 62 yards and found the end zone three times. Michael Penix Jr. threw for 223 yards and a touchdown on 15-of-20 passing.

The Saints' defense has been among the worst in the league this year, and the injuries on Monday only made matters worse. Staley will look to put together a better performance against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday.

articles.title: Eagles flying to London for game vs. Jaguars on Friday, leaving little time to adjust after Rams' issues in Australia
articles.summary: The Rams tried an "in and out" strategy earlier this season in Australia, which is much further than London, and it didn't work out well.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles are following in Sean McVay's footsteps.

The Eagles are set to take on the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday in London. But instead of traveling to the United Kingdom early, head coach Nick Sirianni revealed on Monday that his team is going at about the last possible moment.

They are going to practice at home all week, and then leave on Friday. That plan, Sirianni said, via The Athletic , "felt like the best thing for our team, taking everything into account — jet lag, included."

Now, it's not that big of a difference from Philadelphia to London. It's a roughly seven-hour flight across the Atlantic Ocean, and London is five hours ahead. That means that, once the Eagles land on Friday night, they'll have all day Saturday to adjust before the game starts at 2:30 p.m. local time on Sunday at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

While there is no right way to prepare for an international game like this, travel plans have been called into question after McVay and the Los Angeles Rams opted to fly down to Australia for their season opener against the San Francisco 49ers at the last possible moment. The Rams ended up spending roughly 30 hours in the country between their two flights, something the team had been working on for more than a year.

Then the 49ers, who landed several days in advance, rolled to an easy 27-7 win in Melbourne.

The Eagles will enter Sunday's game with a 2-2 record, and are coming off back-to-back losses. They blew a 10-point fourth quarter lead to the Rams on Sunday, and are likely down both running backs Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby. Beating the Jaguars (3-1), who have won two straight and are preparing for back-to-back games in London over the next two weeks, isn't going to be an easy task regardless of where the game is held or how the Eagles get there.

But if things go poorly, it's easy to wonder how long coaches will keep pushing the "in and out" travel strategy for international games.

articles.title: Los Saints pierden contra los Falcons en el vigésimo aniversario de su vuelta al Superdome tras el Katrina
articles.standfirst: La cantante Irma Thomas, que interpretó el himno nacional en aquel partido, volvió a hacerlo 20 años después
articles.summary: La cantante Irma Thomas, que interpretó el himno nacional en aquel partido, volvió a hacerlo 20 años después
articles.body: Los Atlanta Falcons dominaron a los New Orleans Saints (45-24) en la NFL, en una noche en la que la franquicia de Louisiana recordaba el vigésimo aniversario de su regreso al Superdome tras la devastación causada por el huracán Katrina. Atlanta igualó su récord de cinco touchdowns por carrera. Bijan Robinson sumó 145 yardas y dos anotaciones, y Brian Robinson Jr. aportó 62 yardas y tres 'touchdowns'. El quarterback Michael Penix Jr. lanzó para 223 yardas, con un pase de anotación y ninguna intercepción. Drake London lideró las recepciones con cinco para 96 yardas. Para Nueva Orleans, Tyler Shough acumuló 286 yardas de pase, un touchdown y ninguna intercepción. Alvin Kamara lideró por tierra con 23 yardas y dos anotaciones, mientras que Chris Olave destacó con ocho recepciones para 116 yardas. Atlanta golpeó desde el inicio con una carrera de 59 yardas de Bijan Robinson hasta la zona de anotación. El corredor volvió a marcar antes del cierre del primer cuarto y los Falcons tomaron una ventaja de 14-0, lo que dejó contra las cuerdas a Nueva Orleans. Alvin Kamara recortó distancias al comenzar el segundo período, pero Atlanta respondió con su dominio por tierra. Brian Robinson Jr. anotó y Nick Folk amplió la diferencia hasta el 24-7 al descanso. Los Saints volvieron a sumar en el tercer cuarto, aunque otro 'touchdown' de Brian Robinson frenó sus esperanzas. Nueva Orleans se acercó al 31-17, pero un pase de 31 yardas de Michael Penix Jr. a Jahan Dotson alejó cualquier amenaza. Brian Robinson completó posteriormente su tercer touchdown y elevó la ventaja al 45-17. Los Saints maquillaron finalmente el resultado con una anotación tardía para el definitivo 45-24. Los Saints y los Falcons conmemoraron el vigésimo aniversario del regreso de la franquicia al Superdome después del huracán Katrina, con un programa especial antes y durante el partido. La ceremonia contó con la presencia de varios integrantes del equipo de 2006, entre ellos Drew Brees y Steve Gleason, quien ejerció como capitán honorario y participó en el tradicional 'Who Dat!' previo al encuentro. La cantante Irma Thomas, que interpretó el himno nacional en aquel partido, volvió a hacerlo veinte años después. La celebración incluyó además distintos homenajes a los jugadores y entrenadores de aquel equipo y actuaciones musicales durante el descanso, con Trombone Shorty & Orleans Avenue como protagonistas y la participación de varios artistas vinculados a Nueva Orleans. El 25 de septiembre de 2006, los Saints recibieron a los Falcons en su primer partido en el Superdome después de que Katrina obligara a la franquicia a abandonar temporalmente Nueva Orleans. En el primer cuarto, Gleason bloqueó un despeje de Atlanta en una jugada que terminó con un balón recuperado en la zona de anotación y se convirtió en una de las imágenes más recordadas de la historia de la ciudad. Los Saints se impusieron por 23-3 en un encuentro que simbolizó el regreso de Nueva Orleans a uno de sus principales escenarios deportivos poco más de un año después de la devastación causada por el huracán.
