articles.title: NFL Panic Meter: Eagles offense, Lions defense are big problems for 2 marquee NFC teams
articles.summary: Two of the NFC's marquee teams might already be in trouble.
articles.body:
The two powerhouse teams in the NFC two seasons ago were the 15-2 Detroit Lions, and a Philadelphia Eagles team that went on to win a Super Bowl.

The NFL moves fast. It's only four games into this season but the Eagles and Lions both look incredibly flawed, for different reasons. The Eagles can't move the ball and the Lions can't stop anyone. Both teams can blame injuries, though there are personnel issues too.

The Eagles played most or all of Sunday's game against the Rams without running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring), receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), tight end Dallas Goedert and right tackle Lane Johnson (personal reasons). That's arguably the Eagles' three best skill-position players and their best lineman. Without them they gained 172 yards, averaged just 3 yards per play and blew a 10-point lead in the final five minutes. Not great.

Barkley will be week-to-week with his injury and backup Tank Bigsby is going on injured reserve for a core muscle injury. There is no explanation for what's going on with Johnson.

Head coach Nick Sirianni is getting a lot of criticism. Quarterback Jalen Hurts is catching some too; he hasn't played well all season and wasn't great last season either. The offense seems to miss the presence of A.J. Brown, who was traded this offseason. Next up for the Eagles is a tough game at London against the Jaguars. Hurts, who had only 10 yards passing in the second half on Sunday, probably isn't in danger of losing his job if he continues to play poorly. The Eagles just switched backup quarterbacks, demoting Andy Dalton for Tanner McKee. The fact that both have been No. 3 on the depth chart already this season indicates neither one is threatening Hurts no matter how bad he plays. But a productive game would be a reprieve.

There's a way out of the mess for the Eagles, once they start to get healthy. That might not be the case for the Lions.

The Lions have been in prime time twice. Both times a big audience got to see a team that can still move the ball fine but can't get a stop. The Carolina Panthers look much better on offense in Bryce Young's fourth season, but after punting on their first drive here were the Panthers' next six drives: touchdown, touchdown, field goal, touchdown, touchdown, field goal. The Lions are last in the NFL in yards allowed per game and last in points allowed per game. For those who prefer advanced stats, they're last in EPA ( expected points added ) per play allowed, 29th in success rate allowed and 31st in DVOA . The Lions' offense is top eight in all those stats; that group isn't the problem.

Lions head coach Dan Campbell said he and the Lions knew the Panthers would go to receiver Tetairoa McMillan often with No. 2 receiver Jalen Coker out due to injury. The Lions did nothing to stop him though. He had 14 catches for 192 yards and two touchdowns.

At this point the Lions' defensive issues seem unfixable. A coordinator change can't turn everything around, but Campbell was asked if replacing Kelvin Sheppard was on the table.

"I'm not talking about all that," Campbell said . "I'm talking about getting better right now with what we've got. And that's what we're gonna do. We're going to find a way to get better with what we got."

Cornerback D.J. Reed defended Sheppard, saying after Sunday's game "It's not a coaching thing, it's a players' thing." He might be right, and that brings another set of problems. They're without starting safeties Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch, and also lost defensive back Avonte Maddox to a season-ending injury. Add in the loss of Terrion Arnold, who was cut this offseason after he was arrested, and the Lions secondary is a shell of what it was. At least Branch is "very close" to a return, according to Campbell. Joseph's return doesn't seem imminent. Branch is a good player but even if he returns soon it's not like one safety completely fixes a defense allowing 423.8 yards and 31.8 points per game.

Panic meter: A bad defense seems like it might ruin the Lions season. The same could be true for the Eagles and their offense, though there's some slight hope for a rebound.

In four games the Broncos have 13 first-half points. That's the second-fewest in the NFL through four games over the last five seasons, according to Josh Dubow of the Associated Press . The 2023 Giants had just nine first-half points through four weeks.

The early problems indicate the script to open the game is not working. That's one of the many problems with the Broncos offense.

Denver has struggled with Sean Payton giving play-calling to offensive coordinator Davis Webb to start the season. Payton has been asked regularly since a terrible Week 1 performance what he thinks of the play-calling, or if he'll take it back. Payton has not given any indication that he will do that. But it will be hard to resist if the offensive problems persist.

"I think the frustrations just come within the losses," quarterback Bo Nix said, according to the Broncos' transcripts. "Obviously, we want to have a really explosive offense and that'll come, but we've played really good teams."

The Broncos have played good teams: Chiefs, Jaguars, Rams and 49ers. That doesn't completely excuse an offense that is 27th in yards per game this season. Something better change soon, or the play-caller will change.

Panic meter: It's early, the Broncos are in decent shape at 2-2, but there are a lot of warning signs.

The doctors on social media were in overdrive on Sunday, trying to diagnose Jackson's latest injury. Most of them speculated that it was a mild high ankle sprain.

That's not great for Jackson, but any injury for the Baltimore Ravens quarterback is bad news. We saw how the Ravens' season fell apart last year when Jackson suffered a hamstring injury and wasn't the same when he came back. It doesn't seem like a big deal, but it's worth keeping in mind because another significant injury to Jackson changes the entire NFL landscape.

Panic meter : No worries yet. Hopefully.

Jacoby Brissett is good enough to run a competent offense. He's also not good enough to make a big difference for the Arizona Cardinals when it comes to winning games.

The Cardinals are 2-14 over the last two seasons when Brissett starts. On Sunday, the Cardinals played a Giants team they could have beaten, but Brissett threw three interceptions, including one on the final play that was returned for a touchdown.

Soon, Brissett will face a series of problems. The Cardinals are realistically going to be out of the playoff race quickly. He hasn't played well enough that the Cardinals would keep starting him despite the losses. He's 33 years old and clearly not the future. The Cardinals have a third-round rookie, Carson Beck, who played well in the Hall of Fame game in the preseason and probably needs a longer look before the end of the season. All of that adds up to a quarterback change sooner rather than later.

Panic meter: Brissett needs to play better quickly, and even that might not be enough.

Had Sunday's Rams-Eagles game ended with five minutes left, the conversations this week would have been intense.

The Rams trailed by 10 points and looked to be on the way to a 1-3 start. Matthew Stafford threw two interceptions, giving him six in four games. He had eight all last season. The Rams can't even blame the offensive issues on injuries. They were reasonably healthy. And while the Eagles have a good defense in theory, they were six days removed from being picked apart by Case Keenum, the 38-year-old Bears third-string quarterback.

The Rams saved themselves a week of angst. They scored two late touchdowns to win. They're 2-2, which isn't great, but it's a lot better than 1-3. The Rams get a tough test against the Bills on Monday night in Week 5. Los Angeles avoided a week of grief with a win Sunday, but falling to 2-3 with a loss to the Bills might spark up the discussion about how good the Rams actually are.

Panic meter: The thought that the Rams might just not be great this season is creeping in.

images.caption: Jalen Hurts of the Philadelphia Eagles had a very quiet second half in a loss to the Rams. (Mitchell Leff via Getty Images)

articles.title: ‘Light Years Better With Michael Penix Jr.,’ ‘NFC South Is Unpredictable (and Gross)’ — NFL Analysts React to Falcons’ Dominant Win vs. Saints
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons ran wild on the road, dominating the New Orleans Saints 45-24 on Monday Night Football, improving to 2-2 and tying the Carolina Panthers...
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons ran wild on the road, dominating the New Orleans Saints 45-24 on Monday Night Football, improving to 2-2 and tying the Carolina Panthers for first place in the NFC South.

PFN's analysts had more than a few things to say as the Falcons ran riot in primetime.

NFL Analysts Take Notice After Falcons' Blowout Win

The Falcons' offense has undergone a remarkable turnaround with quarterback Michael Penix Jr. under center after looking like one of the worst teams in the NFL before his return from injury in Week 3.

Against the Saints in Week 4, Bijan Robinson once again impressed, rushing for 145 yards and two touchdowns, while Brian Robinson Jr. added three rushing scores.

PFN's Alex Kennedy noted how the Falcons' offense has opened up with Penix Jr. after a difficult outing with Cooper Rush at quarterback, while Tua Tagovailoa also remained sidelined in the first two weeks.

"The NFC South is always pretty unpredictable (and gross), but I think the Falcons have as good a shot as any team to win this division. At the moment, it feels like a two-team race between Atlanta and Carolina. The Falcons look like a different team with Michael Penix Jr. under center instead of Cooper Rush, though," he wrote.

Brandon Austin, like Kennedy, believes the Falcons have improved their chances as contenders for the division title with Penix Jr. under center, saying, "The NFC South is a roller-coaster ride, but the Falcons should be squarely in the mix for a division title. This team has been light-years better with a healthy Michael Penix Jr."

Meanwhile, Jacob Infante wasn't fully convinced about crowning Atlanta yet, wanting a better look at the team over the next few weeks before coming to a conclusion.

"Michael Penix Jr. deserves a ton of credit for rejuvenating a Falcons team that looked like the worst in the NFL before he came back from injury," Infante said. "I'm hesitant to crown the Falcons as a legitimate contender in the NFC until I see what they can do against top competition, but they've at least shown that they're definitely a contender in the NFC South."

Penix Jr. was ranked fifth in PFN's QB Impact score with a grade of 83.9 in his return game in Week 3 against the Green Bay Packers. In Week 4, he threw for 223 yards, completing 15-for-20 passes, including one touchdown. He finished Week 4 with an 82.7 Impact Score.

Bijan Robinson also praised the Falcons QB's impact, saying : "Huge. A lot. You can't really put 8 in the box… you just don't know if we're gonna run or pass."

"Winning the South might mean not losing it, and this Falcons team can do that with a QB who is willing to feed his two stars and a defense that creates pressure without needing to bring help," Kyle Soppe wrote. "This division isn't likely to get a playoff win, but the rules state that they get a minimum of one playoff team and Atlanta seems poised to be that squad."

The PFN Playoff Meter currently gives them a 23.4% chance of making the playoffs, projecting a seven-win season for the Falcons. Atlanta was ranked 26th in PFN's Offense Impact score with a 70.0 grade through three weeks. After blowing out the Saints in primetime, that grade is now at 78.7 (#8 in the league).

Another PFN analyst, Jason Katz, also wants to look at how the Falcons fare against quality opposition in the coming weeks before reaching a verdict about their division chances.

"Not quite ready to crown the Falcons, but at worst, they're the second-best team in the NFC South. Really impressive two weeks from Michael Penix Jr. Let's see how they do against a top-tier team first," Katz wrote.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Caleb Yaccarino highlighted the volatility among teams in the division, questioning whether an NFC South team like the Falcons can remain consistent throughout the season.

"This is the NFC South we are talking about. One week a team could look incredible, and the next fans are looking at the top prospects in the draft after a horrible loss. It's too early to call the Falcons legit, especially when they went against a heavily injured and struggling Saints defense."

Falcons still have plenty to prove before they can be considered legitimate contenders beyond the NFC South. They will have an opportunity to see where they really stand over the next three weeks with matchups against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 5, the Chicago Bears in Week 6, and an unbeaten San Francisco 49ers in Week 7.

articles.title: Why Packers’ Matt LaFleur is not too interested in engaging in trash talk with Bears
articles.summary: Few rivalries in the NFL can match the history and intensity of the game between the Green Bay Packers and Chicago Bears. The league’s oldest rivalry will be...
articles.body:
Few rivalries in the NFL can match the history and intensity of the game between the Green Bay Packers and Chicago Bears. The league's oldest rivalry will be renewed in Week 5 at Lambeau Field as the Bears travel to Green Bay for a pivotal NFC North showdown, but Packers head coach Matt LaFleur has no interest in adding fuel to the rivalry through trash talk.

When asked about the Packers-Bears rivalry during Monday's press conference, LaFleur said that his attention remains firmly on the players who will actually decide the outcome on the field.

"Because this game is about players, and so we'll keep it about the players. You know I'm not the one out there they're playing, so I think that's always been my mentality, and we're going to keep it about those guys," LaFeur said via Rob Demovsky.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Bears enter the matchup riding back-to-back victories, including a dominant 23-12 win over the New York Jets in Week 4. LaFleur also expressed his appreciation for the historic rivalry while weighing in on the challenge presented by a Chicago team that has started to build momentum.

"Don't get me wrong, I love the rivalry. It's awesome, it's great, it's intense, you can feel it on game day, you can feel it throughout the course of the week, and also the significance. They're the defending North champions, so what a great opportunity for us in our home stadium to play against the defending champs."

Over the decades, the Packers and Bears have produced countless memorable encounters. The rivalry has survived numerous changes throughout the NFL, yet its importance has never faded.

The emotional significance of Packers-Bears remains intact because the matchup represents much more than two teams meeting twice every season. It connects the modern NFL to its earliest history.

As long as Green Bay and Chicago remain in the same division, the NFL's oldest rivalry will likely continue. Now, it remains to be seen which team will emerge victorious this time and add another memorable moment to this historic rivalry.

articles.title: ‘I Messed Up,’ ‘Shedeur Sanders Is Definitely Better’ — Ex-NFL DT Rips Tyler Shough’s Shaky Performance in Falcons vs. Saints
articles.summary: Tyler Shough and the New Orleans Saints fell to 1-3 following a blowout 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons. New Orleans failed to find any offensive rhythm fr...
articles.body:
Tyler Shough and the New Orleans Saints fell to 1-3 following a blowout 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons.

New Orleans failed to find any offensive rhythm from the start, and Shough also found himself on the receiving end of criticism from former defensive tackle Breiden Fehoko after he failed to get the Saints going in primetime.

Breiden Fehoko Changes His Tune on Tyler Shough

In the Week 4 loss to the Falcons, the Saints quickly found themselves in a 14-point hole in the opening quarter. They fell 24-7 at halftime before ultimately suffering a heavy loss.

Shough also faced heavy pressure throughout the game and was sacked twice. Much of his statistical production came after the game was already out of grasp.

Shough connected with DeVaughn Vele for a three-yard touchdown with approximately two minutes remaining, while also leading a pair of 13-play drives in the fourth quarter.

The performance, though, was particularly disappointing for Fehoko, who was extremely confident in Shough heading into the matchup. Before the game, Fehoko even posted that fans would get to watch "the best quarterback in the NFC" play football.

However, Fehoko quickly changed his assessment after Week 4 Monday Night Football.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

"I was so wrong about Tyler Shough. He's not it. Shedeur Sanders is definitely better than this cat," Fehoko tweeted.

Fehoko later acknowledged his previous comment in which he had called Shough the best quarterback in the NFC. "I messed up," Fehoko said.

Shough ended the night completing 30 of 48 passes for 286 yards and one touchdown. He also rushed twice for five yards, but his production was not enough to prevent the Saints from falling badly. His 75.6 PFN QB Impact Score ranks #17 in the league among 34 qualifying quarterbacks.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

Fehoko also later revealed his current NFC South quarterback rankings, placing Shough third behind Bryce Young and Michael Penix Jr., while putting Baker Mayfield fourth.

Shough had previously delivered a stronger performance in the Saints' 35-27 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, throwing four touchdowns. Against Atlanta, he also recorded his second interception-free performance over his last three games, but he has also been sacked 12 times through four games.

Following the loss to Atlanta, Shough remained focused on how the Saints can respond rather than dwelling on the defeat. He acknowledged that the team could eventually look back at the game as a difficult moment, but added the importance of continuing to move forward and learning from the experience.

New Orleans will now have to regroup quickly, as the Saints' next challenge comes against the Minnesota Vikings and their Brian Flores-led defense.

articles.title: NFL 2026 results and highlights: Bijan Robinson stars as Atlanta Falcons blow away New Orleans Saints 45-24 in second win of NFL season
articles.summary: Bijan Robinson scores two rushing touchdowns while Brian Robinson runs in three as the Atlanta Falcons beat the New Orleans Saints 45-24; watch the second NFL London game of the season between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Philadelphia Eagles at 2.30pm Sunday, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell was among those in attendance on the night as New Orleans commemorated the 20th anniversary of the Superdome's reopening after Hurricane Katrina.

Brian Robinson ran for three short touchdowns for the Falcons (2-2), who never trailed and controlled the line of scrimmage while outgaining the Saints (1-3) on the ground, 207 yards to 50.

Atlanta continued rolling behind quarterback Michael Penix Jr, who returned to the lineup for a 35-14 victory at Green Bay. Penix was an efficient 15 of 20 for 223 yards and a touchdown. His 31-yard scoring strike to Jahan Dotson in the fourth quarter would prompt a mass exodus of Saints fans.

Passing: Michael Penix Jr, 15/20, 223 yards, 1 TD

Rushing: Bijan Robinson, 19 carries, 145 yards, 2 TDs

Brian Robinson Jr., 14 carries, 62 yards, 3 TDs

Receiving: Drake London, 5 catches, 96 yards

Passing: Tyler Shough, 30/48, 268 yards, 1 TD

Rushing: Alvin Kamara, 7 carries, 23 yards, 2 TDs

Receiving: Chris Olave, 8 catches, 116 yards

Saints running back Alvin Kamara scored his first two touchdowns of the season, the second cutting Atlanta's lead to 31-17 early in the fourth quarter.

Tyler Shough passed for 286 yards and a late touchdown to Devaughn Vele.

The game kicked off following festivities commemorating the Saints' return to the Superdome after Katrina had displaced the team from New Orleans for the entire 2005 season. In addition to causing levee breaks and a storm surge that flooded about 80 per cent of the city, the hurricane also ripped a hole in the Superdome's roof while evacuees sheltered there.

Ignited by Steve Gleason's punt block for a touchdown following the 2006 game's opening possession, the Saints beat the Falcons 23-3 in that Week 3, Monday night matchup.

Like that meeting two decades ago, the Falcons, wearing red, received the opening kickoff. This time, however, there would be no punt to block. Bijan Robinson burst through a hole on the left side of the line and raced 59 yards for a touchdown.

For a fourth time in four games, the Saints were playing from behind early - a challenge made more difficult by Daniel Carlson's missed 52-yard field goal attempt and running back Kendre Miller's lost fumble on the New Orleans 22-yard line one possession later.

Atlanta cashed in on the turnover when Bijan Robinson made it 14-0 on a 4-yard power run, set up in part by cornerback Kool-Aid McKinstry's third-down defensive holding penalty.

New Orleans Saints WR Devaughn Vele had six catches (on nine targets) for 54 yards and a touchdown during the team's Week 4 loss to the Atlanta Falcons .

Why It Matters: Vele has been solid to open 2026, and he made some nice plays on Monday night. articles.title: NFL: Officials Jeff Seeman and Adrian Hill suspended for player incidents
articles.summary: The NFL suspends officials Jeff Seeman and Adrian Hill for instances of unprofessional conduct towards a player.
articles.body:
The NFL has suspended two officials for instances of unprofessional conduct towards a player.

Line judge Jeff Seeman has been suspended for two games and referee Adrian Hill for one fixture following the incidents on Sunday.

Seeman was caught on camera seeming to curse at Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride, whose side lost 36-24 away to the New York Giants.

McBride felt he had been interfered with by Giants cornerback Dru Phillips from a pass from Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett that fell incomplete.

Having been hit, McBride complained to Seeman, who appeared to yell a profanity at McBride.

"It's a tough one for me. You hate to see it for obvious reasons. I don't need to go further than that, but I do want to give the man a little bit of grace too," Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Monday.

"I know Jeff. He's a good man. It's unfortunate it happened. It can't happen obviously and I'll leave it at that."

Hill's incident involved linebacker Eric Wilson, who featured for Minnesota Vikings as they defeated the visiting Miami Dolphins 15-10.

Wilson was pushed into Hill by Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon II midway through the first quarter after a play was whistled dead because of a Minnesota penalty.

As Wilson tried to help Hill up, the official jumped up while pointing and shouting at Wilson to move away.

"That was funny, honestly," Wilson told reporters after the match.

"I ended up apologising to him and explained the situation. He was cool about it. He understood what was going on. He just said he didn't want us fighting."

In Monday night's fixture, the Atlanta Falcons won 45-24 on the road at the New Orleans Saints.

Bijan Robinson scored an early touchdown following a 53-yard run, while fellow running back Brian Robinson Jr. also reached the end zone three times.

The Falcons now sit second in NFC South, following two opening defeats with consecutive victories, while the Saints are third with a 1-3 record.
